education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the

1- Scope— Specifies the dimensionSp tolerances, tangential loads and other details of T-rings 
(keystone rings 15°) from 82 up to 200 mm nominal diameter for internal combustion engines. 

2. Dimensions and Tolerances — Shall be as given in Table 1 read with Fig. 1, 




Oi-n 



DETAIL A 
SHOWING CHAMFERING OF 
INTERNAL EDGES (Kl) 

All dimensions in millimetres. 
FIG. 1 DIMENSIONS FOR T-RINGS 15^ 

3. Designation — Shall Include: 

a) Type of ring, 

b) Nominal diameter rfi, 

c) Axial width hi, 

d) Number of this standard, 

e) Material symbol, 

f) Manufacturing process, 

g) Whether inside edges chamfered ( Kl ), and 
h) Type of coating. 

Example: 

A keystone ring 15° (T-ring) of a nominal diameter (/i = 90 mm, axial width //| «= 2'5 mm, 
made of S. G. iron (A6), with inside chamfered edges (Kl) and coated with tin all over 
( SN ) shall be designated as: 

T-Ring 90 X 25 IS : 8422 ( Part III ) A6 Kl SN 

4. General Requirements— Shall be as given in IS:5791-1977 'Technical supply conditions for 
piston rings for IC engines (first revision ) \ 

5- Marking — The rings which are to be fitted in a particular direction shall be marked with the word 
* TOP ' on the top sides of the rings. For other markings reference should be made to IS : 5791-1977. 

5.1 ISI Certification A/farA//?g — Details available with the Indian Standards Institution.

IS:8422( Part ill)- 1977 



EXPLANATORY NOTE 



This standard is one of the series of Indian Standards on piston ring dimensions, tangential 
force, etc. 18:5791-1977 is a necessary adjunct to this standard which gives details of materials, 
surface finish, gap types and sizes, surface coatings, manufacturing processes, etc. 

In the preparation of this standard due consideration has been given to the prevalent sizes In 
the industry. It is recommended that for new designs, only the sizes given in this standard be used. 

In the preparation of this standard assistance has been derived from DIN 70914 * Piston rings 
for automotive engineering, T-rings 15', keystone rings IS"" from 82 up to 200 mm nominal diameter ' 
issued by DIN Deutsches Institut fiirNormung. 



Raproduced^by Reprography Unit, ISI New Delhi
